text:
Lighthouses are tall structures, typically built near the shore, equipped with a bright light at the top to serve as a navigational aid for maritime pilots at sea or in inland waterways.
They often feature a distinctive architectural style, such as a cylindrical or conical tower, designed to withstand harsh coastal weather and provide a clear line of sight for the light beam.
The light source within a lighthouse, historically an oil lamp and now often an electric bulb or LED, is amplified by a lens system, such as a Fresnel lens, to project a beam visible for many miles.
